Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with shortness of breath that has been slowly worsening over the last couple of weeks.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: I'm, contacting you because I've been, quite short of breath lately... well it seems to have been, slowly getting worse over the last couple of weeks.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Shortness of breath has become particularly troublesome in the last few days, now occurring with minimal exertion like walking around the house.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: now it's, become quite troublesome, in the last few days... now I'm having to sort of sit down and catch my breath. And I'm really starting to get a bit breathless, just about the house.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports bilateral ankle swelling (edema) for the past few days.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I've noticed my ankles have got a bit bigger... Uh, it's just like, it's sort of swollen up a bit... yeah, both ankles... I kind of noticed it the last few days.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has a mild, non-troublesome dry cough.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Uh, I've got a bit of a dry cough, but it's not too troublesome.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies chest pain, palpitations, and fever.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: No pain in my chest... have you noticed your heartbeat racing at all? So, palpitations or skipped heartbeat? No, not really... any temperatures or fevers? Uh, no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient feels a little run-down but otherwise normal, with a normal appetite and fluid intake.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I'm feeling a little run-down, um, but otherwise, otherwise pretty normal... Yeah, I, , I'm, that's fine.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports polyuria (peeing a lot), which he attributes to his diuretic medication.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I usually pee a lot, , ever since the drugs .

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has a known history of heart failure.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: I've, I've uh, I've got um, heart failure.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient had a 'small heart attack' about five years ago, which was described as more than angina.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: well I was told I had like a, they called it like a small heart attack... About, five years ago... Uh, no they, they said that it, uh, it seemed, it was like, more than angina.

Medications.source_text: Uh, yeah, I take something called Furosemide.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Any allergies at all? Any medications? Uh, no, no allergies.

Family_History.content: Father died of a heart attack in his early sixties.
Family_History.source_text: my, my father died of a, uh, of a heart attack... he was, um, early sixties.

Family_History.content: Mother has osteoporosis and is still living.
Family_History.source_text: my mother had osteoporosis... Uh, yeah, she's still living.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient lives alone with two cats.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Uh, I live on my own. Well, I got two cats.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works part-time as a lorry driver, working only day shifts.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Uh, I work part-time as, a, uh, lorry driver... I only take shifts during the day, I don't like working at night.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is an ex-smoker with a 25-pack-year history (one pack a day for 25 years).
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Not any more... it was about, about a pack a day... good twenty five years.

Assessment.content: The impression is an exacerbation (flare-up) of heart failure.
Assessment.source_text: based on you history, and having listened to your story, I, I wonder whether you've had a flare-up of your heart failure, sir.

Plan_of_Care.content: Increase Furosemide dose to one tablet twice a day for a few days.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I'm quite happy to increase your dose of Furosemide. Maybe, rather than one tablet a day, we can do two tablets a day, for the first few days.

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange blood tests, including a full blood count (FBC) and kidney function (U+Es).
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Let's, let's get a blood test done. We can check your um, you know your full blood count... We can have a check of your kidney function.

Plan_of_Care.content: Arrange an echocardiogram to assess heart function.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: what we should also think about is maybe doing a couple of other tests... maybe an echocardiogram of your heart, to see how well your heart's pumping.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review in one week's time.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: But I really like, would like you to come back and see me in about a week's time, see how you're getting on.

Follow_up_Information.content: Advised to seek urgent review sooner if getting more unwell, more breathless, or develops chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: if you are getting more unwell, feel like you're getting more breathless, or you're having any other symptoms like chest pain, or palpitations or dizziness, then, uh, you know I want you to give me a call sooner
